experiments.title: C1 — the epitope triage on the apical domain
experiments.summary: 96 Genie 3 and 121 hosted RFD4-Proteina designs across four apical patches. The standard co-fold screen is blind on this target — proven with controls — so a directed restrained read decided: the conserved dual-anchor patch advances, one design short for the organizers' tip.
experiments.goal: Choose the epitope for the binder build with a pre-registered rule, on a screen validated with controls.
goal_extra: Strategy difference: the only campaign whose deliverable is a decision, not designs - it judges epitopes (four apical patches, two generator arms) and every later campaign inherits that choice. The others each vary one axis of the work; C1 picks the ground they are built on.
Answers: which of the four apical patches produces dockable interfaces?
Answers: can any co-fold screen be trusted on this target?
experiments.verdict_detail: Controls: the challenge-2 champion reproduces at ipSAE 0.84-0.90 through the same pipeline, while the native B19 virus RBD floats 42-55 A from the verified footprint in both Boltz-2 and Chai-1. Directed re-read (Chai-1 pocket restraints): the conserved dual-anchor patch puts 8 of 24 designs at or above 0.45 (top 0.752, above the native reference's 0.42-0.48); the organizers' tip gets 5 of 24 — one short of the line, not eliminated, stable on a second seed. The two other patches carry no restrained read by recorded decision.

chapters.title: G — four patches, two generators
chapters.text: 96 local Genie 3 backbones (CA-only MPNN sequences) and 121 hosted RFD4-Proteina designs spanning the organizers' tip, two conserved patches and a conserved dual-anchor pair.

steps.title: Sequence the local arm with ProteinMPNN

chapters.outcome: 220 designs, all on-patch by construction.

chapters.title: V — the blind screen, proven with controls
chapters.text: 495 co-fold samples were read against the designed patches before anything was believed: the known-good control reproduces, and the native virus binder refuses to dock.

steps.title: Fold the challenge-2 champion control — reproduces at ipSAE 0.84-0.90
Fold the native B19 RBD — floats 42-55 A away, ipSAE 0.000
Re-check the footprint straight from the experimental structure (auth 202-212 + 348/371)

chapters.outcome: The unrestrained read is fold-limited on this target: recorded as cannot-decide, not as an epitope verdict.

chapters.title: R — the directed re-read
chapters.text: With the interface directed by pocket restraints, the same models dock designs at their designed patch and rank them — the first read that discriminates.

steps.title: Calibrate on the native complex: directed ipTM 0.42-0.48
Screen 48 triage designs (five samples each, stable within +-0.02)
Falsify the restraint-count confound (equal-bars rerun, no jump)

chapters.outcome: A rankable, directed consistency read; caveat recorded: directed, not independent binding evidence.

chapters.title: D — the decision
chapters.text: The registered rule (25 percent of a set at or above 0.45, level with the native reference) applied to the full data, guards on.

steps.title: Apply the guarded rule: the conserved dual-anchor patch advances
Settle the margin with a second seed: the tip stays one short

chapters.outcome: Binder build runs on the conserved dual-anchor patch; the tip is carried as a secondary, not eliminated.

experiments.title: C2 — the binding families and their generator arms
experiments.summary: Batch-2 generation on the surviving epitope: 32 Genie 3 + 49 hosted RFD4-Proteina designs, every one folded on the restrained read (405 samples). 20 cleared the line — 17 at or above 0.50, top e12rfd4_r5d1 0.779. No separation between the arms (Fisher p = 0.605).
experiments.goal: Turn the surviving epitope (E12) into a family: generate batch-2 material with two independent generators and screen every design with the same instrument.
goal_extra: Strategy difference: C2 explores the generator axis - the same E12 site produced through two independent routes (local Genie 3, hosted RFD4) - while C3-C6 act on designs already chosen. It is the only campaign whose variable is who builds the binder, not what is asked of it.
No pre-selection: geometry screen only, then all 81 designs fold.
The 20 clearing the line carry into campaign 3 (switch) and campaign 4 (mouse).
experiments.verdict_detail: The pool is materially stronger than campaign 1's: 17 designs at or above 0.50 against 7, top 0.779 against 0.752, all well above the native reference ceiling (0.48). RFD4 11/49 (22 %), Genie 3 9/32 (28 %) — statistically indistinguishable. Robustness: a host display-driver crash killed one design's fold mid-screen; the pass resumed on driver 621.01 with the allocator workaround and the killed design (r4d3) completed at 0.682.

chapters.title: G — batch-2 generation, two arms
chapters.text: 32 local Genie 3 backbones (CA-only MPNN sequences) and 49 hosted RFD4-Proteina designs, all on the E12 anchors (K344/K374).
chapters.outcome: 81 designs screened; the top reaches 0.779.

chapters.title: R — the restrained screen
chapters.text: 81 designs × 5 samples = 405 folds on the E12 anchors, seed 42, serial on one GPU.

steps.title: Score at-site: worst hotspot distance + binder residues at the site

chapters.outcome: 20 of 81 at or above 0.45 - the family pool clears.

chapters.title: D — 20 carry forward
chapters.text: 20 designs at mean restrained ipTM ≥ 0.45 (17 ≥ 0.50); they carry into the switch layer and the mouse cross-fold.
chapters.outcome: 20 designs forward into the switch layer and the cross-fold.

chapters.title: B — batch-3: the E12 extension and the E3 close
chapters.text: The hosted RFD4 pool was drained further: +24 E12 designs folded (4/24 at the bar, same band as the arm itself) and a triple-cation set E3 = {231, 344, 374} was generated and screened. The E12 extension produced a co-champion — b3_E12_r90003 at 0.776, a statistical tie with r5d1 — plus a second at 0.692. E3 is closed as a measured negative: 9 of its 24 designs were built into the N251 glycan and excluded, and of the 15 that folded only 1/15 reached the bar against the rule's 4 — the 231K corner is glycan-shielded and the wide patch is hard.
chapters.outcome: 39 designs, 195 samples, zero fold failures. Co-champion b3_E12_r90003 (0.776); E3 closed negative.

chapters.title: W — wave 2: the hybrid anchor set
chapters.text: The RFD4 wave (26 folded) and the RFdiffusion arm (16) ran overnight, zero failures. The long-length extension (110-140 aa) did NOT beat the short champions (best engaged read 0.420), but the hybrid set H = {R208, Y211, K344, K374} — the organizers' named patch plus the functional tip — delivered b4_H_r1d0000 = 0.777 (5/5 engaged, champion class) and b4_H_r1d0004 = 0.645. Both entered the c6 top 20. 22 designs above 126 aa stay held (host crash class).
chapters.outcome: New champion-class design on a new epitope footprint: b4_H_r1d0000 0.777.

experiments.title: C3 — the pH switch layer
experiments.summary: 29 histidine variants retrofitted onto the top 10 families (singles, doubles, a 0→3 ladder). 21 kept their binding; the engineered sites register the predicted bound-state pKa depression at the anchor lysines (−0.5…−2.8); far picks read flat; one wrong-direction control. 13 carry into the mouse fold.
experiments.goal: Objective 1: put a pH switch into the binder — a histidine neutral at pH 7.4 and protonated at 6.0, facing an anchor lysine, so binding weakens as the pH falls.
goal_extra: Strategy difference: the only campaign that changes the designs' chemistry rather than their origin or target: engineered histidines aimed at the two switched lysines. C2 varies the generator, C4 the species, C5 the architecture; C3 changes the response to pH - and re-reads every parent with the same instrument, so each variant compares directly to its parent.
Positions picked from the co-folded poses: side chain 3.5–8.5 Å from an anchor NZ, solvent-exposed.
Both anchors are conserved lysines (K344/K374), so the same chemistry serves the mouse objective.
experiments.verdict_detail: The registered sign gate is a consistency check (26/29 move positive; unmodified parents carry a 12 % positive null). The substance is per-site: engineered histidines shift −0.5…−2.8 pKa units when bound; picks at the far window edge (8.0–8.4 Å) read flat and their totals go negative; one site reads +0.48 (wrong direction). Magnitudes are never quoted. The top family's ladder is strictly increasing with histidine count (parent −0.057 → +0.029 → +0.625 → +0.708).

chapters.title: P — picking the positions
chapters.text: For every qualifying design: binder side chains pointing at the anchor lysines (3.5–8.5 Å engage window, relative SASA ≥ 0.20). In the top families these are the carboxylates the generators had already aimed at the anchors.
chapters.outcome: 29 variants built across the kept families.

chapters.title: F — variants, identical treatment
chapters.text: 29 variants (7 doubles, 19 singles, a 3-step ladder) built with the parent's MSA and restraints — the only change is the mutated sequence.
chapters.outcome: 29 folded; 21 kept on the at-site line.

chapters.title: G — gates and the per-site mechanism
chapters.text: Gate 1: binding kept (21/29). Gate 2 (registered): the sign check, reported as consistency. Mechanism: PROPKA pKa bound vs free on every engineered histidine.
chapters.outcome: 13 carry forward; the strongest per-site shift is -2.82 at position 28.

chapters.title: D — 13 carry forward
chapters.text: Carried by gate 1 + geometry + per-site mechanism; the ladder ships as the declared mechanism control.
chapters.outcome: 13 designs carry into selection.

chapters.title: P — pH-conditioned redesign (Proton-PottsMPNN)
chapters.text: The switch layer gains a design-side arm: Proton-PottsMPNN redesigns the interface with explicit protonation-state tokens. Off-label for our direction (the engine's campaigns pin the protonated state; we pinned the neutral HIS-S so the bound complex favours it — release on acidification). First sweep degenerated at high selectivity weight (His/Arg-rich near-homopolymers); the capped rerun (<=12 mutations) gave four sane variants. Best: ppmpnn_r4d5_l01_s0 = 0.752 engaged, 0.008 below its parent while carrying the designed switch.
chapters.outcome: 4 variants, best 0.752 (near-parent) with the switch designed in, not screened after.

experiments.title: C4 — the mouse cross-fold: closing the species gap
experiments.summary: 33 designs (20 C2 + 13 C3) folded against the mouse receptor under the identical protocol; two mouse-competent candidates found. Extended 2026-10-28/29: the pool's mouse coverage now runs to 58 designs (every final design included), which is what the selector's mouse component ranks on.
experiments.goal: Objective 2: does the design intent survive against the mouse receptor? Every human qualifier re-folded on the mouse target, anchors mapped by alignment.
goal_extra: Strategy difference: the only measurement-only campaign - it generates nothing and modifies nothing, folding the other campaigns' designs against the mouse construct under exactly their protocol. Changing only the species (never chemistry, generator or architecture) is what makes the human/mouse delta readable.
Anchors: human K344/K374 → mouse K346/K376 (fold 224/254) — never a fixed offset (the constructs carry an indel).
Mouse target is an AlphaFold model (Q62351, 123–763); the structural asymmetry against the human experimental structure is recorded.
experiments.verdict_detail: Bands (adapted instrument): top ≤ 0.05 — r4d5 (−0.050), r3d4_d2 (+0.018), b2_31 (−0.053); second ≤ 0.15 — b2_29, r4d5_d2, r6d2. The strong human parents r5d1/r5d7/b2_20 fall to 0.36/0.27/0.26 — affinity and cross-transfer read as opposed here. Observation: the histidine retrofits improve the mouse read in most families (r5d7 0.266 → 0.579).

chapters.title: G — the design set enters the cross-fold
chapters.text: The designs carried by campaigns 2 and 3 - and later rounds as they landed (switch variants, the c3b winners, the liability repairs) - each folded against the mouse construct under the same restrained protocol as the human read, so the species delta means something.
chapters.outcome: The paired human/mouse read; 63 designs measured in total.

chapters.title: F — 33 designs against the mouse construct
chapters.text: Target prep scripted: mouse sequence from the AlphaFold model, anchors by alignment, MSA depth 1024, then the identical restrained fold.
chapters.outcome: 33 designs paired; the mouse-competent class identified.

chapters.title: D — the paired read
chapters.text: Human mean vs mouse mean per design; bands fixed before the run.
chapters.outcome: Two mouse-competent candidates recorded; the read feeds every later round.

experiments.title: C5 — two-chain units vs the single-chain class
experiments.goal: Whether splitting the binder unit across two designed chains beats the single-chain class at the E12 patch.
goal_extra: Strategy difference: the only campaign with a second designed chain - every other campaign designs one binder against the target, C5 designs a pair that must also hold each other. Its question is architectural (C3's is chemical, C2's generative), and it stays recorded capability: it proves the assembly, not superiority.
RFD4 generated chains B and C jointly against {344K, 374K}
the unit was read per chain because the assembled fold is unrunnable on this host (VRAM cliff).

chapters.title: G — the hosted endpoint accepts two designed chains
chapters.text: The RFD4 request was extended with a second expandable segment (chain C, entity 2, its own length range). The endpoint accepted it with zero validation errors, 8 designs in 95 seconds. 24 designs were generated; 23/24 form a real B-C unit covering both anchor lysines; 2 designs clashed with the N251 glycan and were excluded; 22 folded.
chapters.outcome: 24 -> 22 designs, 23/24 real two-chain units.

chapters.title: F — the assembled fold refused the host
chapters.text: The three-chain fold sits at 11.9 of 12.2 GB VRAM and runs its trunk ~10x slow (775 s/recycle against an 82 s baseline); two attempts, one on a cold boot, and the first ended in a host crash. The read was taken per chain instead: each design folded twice (chain B and chain C alone, own interface-derived restraints) - 44 folds, all complete. The B-C interface stays validated from the design models. Update 2026-10-29: the block-target rescue ran - all 22 assembled units folded against the 221-res apical block; 19/22 engage both binders at the anchors (74/110 samples) and the B-C brace forms. The direction is no longer untested; only the full-protomer assembled fold remains out of reach here.
chapters.outcome: 44 per-chain folds; protocol adaptation recorded.

chapters.title: D — verdict: untested on this host (closed on cost grounds)
chapters.text: The per-chain proxy reads 0/22 at the registered bar (best mean 0.502; best minimum 0.356) with DockQ vs the design models ~0.1 — but both numbers are the expected result of folding a unit chain without its partner, so they are recorded as inconclusive, not negative. Reviewer finding 1 (2026-10-27) applied: the registered rule's profile conditions were only ever measurable on the assembled fold. A cheap rescue exists: the same 22 units against the 221-residue apical block target (~2.5 h GPU).
chapters.outcome: Closed untested, on cost grounds; per-chain proxy confounded by construction. Block-target rescue recorded, not queued.

chapters.title: D - the block rescue runs: the assembled units assemble
chapters.text: All 22 assembled units folded against the 221-res apical block (Boltz-2, pocket restraints on both binders at the E12 anchors in block numbering 165/195, 5 samples each). 74 of 110 samples engage both binders at the anchors - 19 of 22 designs have at least one, 10 engage in every sample - the designed B-C brace forms (contact 1.8-2.9 A), and the best units read ipTM 0.958 / 0.923 / 0.901. The structure explorer on this page now shows the assembled units.
chapters.outcome: 19/22 designs assemble at the designed interfaces.

experiments.title: C6 — evaluating and refining the finalists
experiments.goal: Decide what deserves the twenty slots - by evaluation and refinement, not by new generation: every candidate gets the same multi-tool read, and weak evidence is repaired away.
goal_extra: Strategy difference: the only campaign that adds no designs of its own - it re-reads what C2-C4 produced (restrained fold, unrestrained re-fold, mouse, ipSAE, novelty, seed and liability checks), ranks it, and refines the survivors with targeted repairs (the switch-transfer round, the sequence-liability repairs). The earlier campaigns ask "what can we make?"; C6 asks "what do we actually know about it?".

chapters.title: S — the selector runs
chapters.text: One script owns the ranking (campaigns/c6-selection/scripts/select-top20.py). First pass: 245 designs scored, 98 fail the floors, 20 selected. Top pick c3_e12rfd4_r4d5_d2 at 95.0 — the mouse-competent champion's switch variant.
chapters.outcome: 245 designs scored; top pick 95.0.

chapters.title: W — wave 2 enters the pool
chapters.text: b4/b4r folded (26/26, 16/16); the ppmpnn arm entered. Final run with the completed data (mouse reads for the whole pool, ipSAE over the top-32, prescreen novelty): 293 scored, 129 fail the floors, 20 selected - 20 distinct backbones, zero duplicates. The champion holds rank 1; the switch arm contributes 7 of the 20.
chapters.outcome: 293 scored; final 20 frozen.

chapters.title: V — the multi-tool confidence matrix
chapters.text: Boltz-2 restrained folds + ipSAE now cover the full top-32 pool (32/32, all poses on-site under the engagement gate). b3_E12_r90003 remains the most cross-validated design (chai 0.776, boltz ipTM 0.808, ipSAE 0.50, pDockQ2 0.43); the r4d5/r5d1 champions carry the top chai reads with low ipSAE - no single in-silico metric decides. Per-design values: records/ipsae-pool-2026-10-28.csv (mean over 5 models). Fill pass complete: the eight final designs outside the top-32 pool are folded and scored too, so all 20 carry the three required screens.
chapters.outcome: 32/32 folded and scored; r90003 leads the agreement table.

chapters.title: N — novelty
chapters.text: binder-prescreen v0.5 target arm: 6,695 TfR1 references; 20/20 pass with no prior-art or known-binder flags (closest sequence similarity 0.28). Structural arm (US-align, coverage-aware): 0/20 hits at TM > 0.5 across > 70% of the design (max 0.14). Within the batch: median pairwise TM 0.37, 8 fold clusters; one pair shares a scaffold at 0.99 (the champion and its Proton-PottsMPNN sibling, different method families - kept deliberately).
chapters.outcome: 20/20 pass the target arm; 0 structural hits; 8 fold clusters.

chapters.title: U - the unrestrained read (the honest test)
chapters.text: Every final design re-folded with no pocket restraints at all (chai, 5 samples). 11 of 20 find the designed site on their own; 5 of them in every sample - b4_H_r1d0000 (0.777), e12_18 (0.767), the champion c3_e12rfd4_r4d5_d2 (0.725), c3_e12rfd4_r5d1_d2 (0.681), b4_H_r1d0004 (0.650). The other 9 read high only under restraints and are restraint-dependent, recorded openly. Explorer: viewers/multiview/c6-unrestrained.html.
chapters.outcome: 11/20 engage unrestrained; 5 at 5/5 including the champion.

chapters.title: T - the switch-transfer round
chapters.text: Ten histidine variants built on the three strongest-binding parents (b4_H_r1d0000, e12_18, b4_H_r1d0004 - the five unrestrained 5/5 designs minus the champion family, which already carries switches). Read on the full stack: restrained folds, unrestrained re-folds, the Wyman linkage, the per-site pKa, the mouse cross-fold, the prescreen. The winner c3_b4_H_r1d0000_53h keeps the parent's binding (restrained 0.768, unrestrained 0.771 at 5/5) and adds a measured switch (2 sites, per-site -2.14, forward direction); its sibling 49h carries the strongest linkage in the project (+1.153, 14.2x) and sits first in the reserve. Two selector fixes landed with the round: the S component now enforces the documented direction gate (a wrong-direction linkage caps S), and a near-neighbour cluster prefers the stronger measured switch inside a 1-point band.
chapters.outcome: 4 variants in the twenty; the hybrid parents succeeded by their switch variants.

chapters.title: Liability repair round
chapters.summary: Screen-and-repair pass over the twenty's sequence liabilities (N-glyc sequons, deamidation motifs, free cysteines; Pythia-inspired). Five repair variants folded restrained, unrestrained and mouse; n10q and n30q replaced their parents at no measured cost, three repairs measurably hurt binding and were held. Swapped list re-passes the prescreen 20/20.
chapters.text: A screen-and-repair pass over the twenty's sequence liabilities (N-glycosylation sequons, deamidation motifs, free cysteines), then conservative repair variants folded restrained, unrestrained and mouse, and put through the organizers' prescreen.
chapters.outcome: n10q and n30q replaced their parents at no measured cost; three repairs held (measured binding cost); the swapped list re-passes the prescreen 20/20.

experiments.verdict: Final: the sequence-repaired twenty stands - 20/20 prescreen, engagement-gated reads, seed- and liability-checked.
experiments.summary: The evaluation and refinement of the pool. Final run: 314 designs scored (the switch-transfer variants and the liability repairs added), 20 selected - 5 at switch class S5, 20/20 prescreen pass. Two refinement rounds changed the set: the b4_H parents replaced by their switch variants (53h: unrestrained 0.771 at 5/5, mouse 0.527, per-site -2.14), and two sequence-liability repairs (n10q, n30q) replacing their parents at no measured cost. Lead candidate unchanged: c3_e12rfd4_r4d5_d2 (95.0).
experiments.verdict_detail: Two interface-liability repairs replaced their parents at no measured cost; the swapped list re-passes the prescreen 20/20. Submission package built.
